svg.title: Rows come from the batch, columns from the last dense layer
svg.desc: The five arrays of the forward pass drawn twice, as bands one column per feature. Top, the batch of 300 spiral points, each band drawn short: X is (300, 2), dense1.output (300, 3), activation1.output (300, 3), dense2.output (300, 3), activation2.output (300, 3). Between the arrays, the four objects: dense1 with weights (2, 3), activation1 with no weights, dense2 with weights (3, 3), activation2 with no weights. A bracket under the last four arrays says that they share the shape (300, 3). Bottom, the same pass on the first 7 rows, drawn row by row: (7, 2), then (7, 3) four times. In every shape the row count is printed in blue and the column count in orange, and the orange column count of each dense layer's weights is the column count of its output.
svg.text: Rows come from the batch, columns from the last dense layer
snippets/shape_audit.py, run on all 300 spiral points and again on the first 7.
All 300 rows, each band drawn short

g.text: four arrays of the same shape, (300, 3): a mix-up between them raises no error

svg.text: The first 7 rows, X[:7], through the same four objects
300, 7: rows, one per point of the batch
2, 3: columns, the features; a dense layer sets them to its neuron count
Section 9 hands dense2 the wrong one of the four; only a check on the values catches it.
